rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Three halogens, three signatures. **Chlorine** is the greenish-yellow gas that bleaches moist litmus quickly and betrays itself to excess ammonia as dense white NH₄Cl fumes. **Bromine** is the red-brown vapour that bleaches slowly and never colours starch.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Chlorine bleaches, bromine browns, iodine blues: the three halogens are identified by what they do to litmus, to water and to starch."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The disappearing blue*** — heat the blue-black starch-iodine mixture and the colour drains away; cool it and the blue returns: the helix complex is physical, not chemical.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Cl2: bleach fast + white NH4Cl fumes. Br2: brown vapour + slow bleach + no starch. I2: starch blue-black + violet sublimate. AgX ladder: white/cream/yellow; NH3 solubility: dil/conc/never.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): How would you distinguish between chlorine, bromine and iodine using chemical tests?** — **Chlorine:** a greenish-yellow gas that bleaches moist litmus rapidly; passed into excess ammonia it gives **dense white fumes of NH₄Cl** (8NH₃ + 3Cl₂ → 6NH₄Cl + N₂); passed into KI solution it liberates iodine, which turns starch…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): A colourless halide solution gives a cream precipitate with AgNO3 that dissolves only in concentrated ammonia. Identify the halide and explain.** — The precipitate is **AgBr** (cream): **Ag⁺ + Br⁻ → AgBr↓**.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Mention that the starch colour is an adsorption (guest-host) complex and is reversible with temperature — that detail lifts the answer.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: One gas, one signature: bleaching speed separates Cl2 from Br2, the starch complex isolates I2, and the AgX colour-plus-ammonia ladder finishes any halide identification — no single test is universal, the combination is.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Cl2: greenish-yellow gas, bleaches moist litmus fast, excess NH3 -> white NH4Cl fumes (8NH3 + 3Cl2 -> 6NH4Cl + N2), liberates I2 from KI. Br2: red-brown vapour, bleaches moist litmus slowly, no starch colour, orange in water, displaces I2 from KI.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The starch-iodine complex is so reliable it serves as the internal indicator in every iodometric titration worldwide.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Why does the blue colour of the starch-iodine complex disappear on heating and reappear on cooling?** — The colour comes from **iodine molecules (I₂/I₃⁻) occupying the helical cavity of amylose**, forming a guest–host charge-transfer complex that absorbs visible light.…

Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why starch turns blue-black with iodine - I₂ (actually I₃⁻ in solution) slips inside the amylose helix of starch; the guest–host charge-transfer complex absorbs visible light, giving the intense blue-black. Heating shakes the complex apart (colour fades); cooling rebuilds it — a reversible, diagnostic colour.…  ·  ## 5.
